scene.summary: Four steep gables, capped blue-gray stacks, cream southwest decks and the stepped wing form a strong, charming silhouette. Siding, trim and detail scale are consistent, with no major visible rendering defects. The principal entrance remains unresolved.

building.summary: The miniature has a coherent, charming style, with staggered roof peaks, muted siding, cream trim and a southeast wing. No obvious rendering defects stand out, but principal-entry placement remains unverified.

building.summary: The steep, low-eaved roof, paired dormers and restrained cottage palette are recognizable and coherent. Principal-entry placement remains unresolved.

scene.summary: The compact cottage reads clearly through its steep, low-eaved roof and paired tall-glazed dormers. Pale siding, cream trim and muted shingles fit the scene’s scale and palette. No obvious major rendering defects; the principal entrance remains provisional.

building.summary: Recognizable roof silhouette, sage-and-cream palette and wraparound veranda, but the upper balconies still read as boarded-up openings.

scene.summary: The broad charcoal roof, intersecting gables, sage siding, cream veranda and recessed wing remain recognizable. orientation.summary: The prior SV3 finding establishes the principal entrance on +v (NW, 310°). building.summary: Recognizable massing, sage siding, garage wing and chimney, but several prominent roof and porch details need refinement.

orientation.summary: SV2 looks southwest toward the northeast (-u, 40°) facade and shows the principal entry beneath a two-story porch; the labeled render and actual double-door inventory agree. Upper balcony access is on that same face. SV4 confirms the southeast (-v, 130°) garage and secondary pedestrian entries, not duplicated principal portals. Its garage-left/gable-right arrangement is preserved, not mirrored.

issues.problem: The two curved dormers have blank sage fronts instead of the characteristic dark arched windows.
issues.fix: Add prominent dark glazing with ivory arched surrounds beneath both curved caps.

issues.problem: The northeast entrance balcony lacks the reference's dominant elevated, deep hipped canopy; the low roof compresses this defining feature.
issues.fix: Raise and deepen the canopy over the right-hand upper balcony, with clearly exposed tall posts and a lower connecting roof to the left wing.

issues.problem: Solid white southeast porch roofs read as awnings rather than the reference's airy pergola.
issues.fix: Replace these slabs with simplified, visibly spaced ivory rafters and beams.

scene.summary: Sage-and-ivory materials, varied roof masses, stone chimney and garage-left/gable-right silhouette work well. The curved dormers still appear blank rather than dark and glazed. The northeast balcony canopy remains low and compressed, while southeast porch roofs still read as solid slabs rather than spaced pergola rafters. These defining repairs are not convincingly visible.

orientation.summary: The prior SV2 finding places the principal entrance on -u (NE, 40°), beneath the two-story porch. The -v garage and two pedestrian doors match the independently established secondary entries from SV4, with the garage-left/gable-right arrangement preserved.

building.summary: Recognizable porch-lined residential row with coherent miniature styling, but the tall blank masonry base substantially changes its downhill appearance.

orientation.summary: Located SV3 looks northwest toward the southeast (+v) porch frontage; SV1 corroborates its sheltered entrances. issues.fix: Replace the exposed tall masonry with gray siding and lower-level windows, retaining only a modest foundation strip. Connect porch landings to the terrain with appropriately descending steps.

scene.summary: Four stacked porch groups, repeated chimneys and rear cross-gables give this row strong identity. The final sheet still shows a tall blank masonry base at the downhill end and across much of the rear, rather than a gray-sided, windowed lower level. Porch landings also lack convincing descending connections to the slope. These remain substantial grounding defects despite the reported repair.

orientation.summary: Prior independent SV3/SV1 findings establish the southeast +v porch frontage. The final inventory agrees: four doors, all on +v at 138°, beneath the four porch groups, with no competing doors on other faces.

building.summary: Recognizable gray-green residence with characteristic ivory balconies and a correctly placed lower wing. The dormer and downhill base need refinement.

orientation.summary: Located SV4 looks northwest toward the southeast-facing −v frontage, showing balconies and residential entries; SV1 and SV2 provide supporting oblique views. The labeled render and actual inventory place all four doors on −v, with no competing portals on other faces. The lower northeast wing is correctly on the right in this frontage view, not mirrored. SV3 chiefly shows an intervening yellow building.

issues.problem: The characteristic glazed dormer reads as a blank, white-sided rooftop box.

issues.problem: The downhill end sits on an oversized exposed masonry plinth, making the residence look elevated on a podium rather than settled into a slope.
issues.fix: Bring surrounding terrain closer to the foundation and step the frontage locally, retaining the lower northeast wing without the tall continuous exposed base.

scene.summary: The long gray-green gabled body, four ivory balconies and lower northeast wing remain recognizable and well scaled. The dormer now shows dark glazing, but its thick white cap still dominates; a thinner fascia would clarify its low shed form. A tall continuous masonry wedge remains conspicuous on the downhill end and rear, leaving the residence podium-like rather than comfortably settled into the slope.

orientation.summary: Prior independent SV4 findings, supported by SV1/SV2, identify the southeast −v entrance frontage. All four final doors are on −v at 133°: two central and one in each end volume. No other face has doors, and the lower northeast wing correctly appears on the right of the frontage.

building.summary: The long gray block, stepped green-gray roof and cream stacked porches form a coherent, recognizable miniature. Principal-entry placement remains unresolved.

orientation.summary: SV3 looks northwest toward +v (SE outward, 134°); SV2 views +v obliquely with the southwest end. scene.summary: The stepped green-gray roof, three cream stacked porch groups, paired end windows and modest foundation make a coherent, charming miniature. No comparably major visual defect stands out, but attractive modeling does not resolve the required entrance check.

orientation.summary: Prior independent SV2/SV3 findings support the southeast +v balcony frontage, not the principal-entry hierarchy. Matching plan coordinates alone do not prove duplicated portals, but neither the sheet nor the supplied findings establishes shared versus independent principal access. The author’s plan explicitly remains unresolved.

building.summary: The low cream cottage, charcoal hip roof and single chimney read well, but the entrance gable still lacks its defining open, raised character.

scene.summary: The low cream cottage, charcoal hipped roof, single chimney, and pale porch posts read well. However, the final -u view still shows a closed pale triangular entrance pediment rather than the characteristic raised, steeper open gable. Remove the triangular infill and make the taller exposed pale framing legible at diorama scale; retain the otherwise successful massing.

orientation.summary: The prior independent finding places the shelter at the southeast end of the northeast (-u) facade, image-left. This matches the source-to-face finding, independently of the author plan or nearest-road hint.

building.summary: The offset brown hips, deep eaves, taller northwest core, low southeast wing and pale rear extension form a coherent, recognizable miniature. No obvious geometry defects or mirrored wings are apparent, but principal-entry placement remains unverified.

building.summary: Recognizable, coherent miniature: stepped brown gables, broad southwest dormer, sheltered entrance and southeast bay capture the defining features. No major visible defects.

building.summary: The muted siding, intersecting gables and northeast terraces create a coherent miniature, but principal-entry placement remains unverified.

orientation.summary: Prior independent findings support the NNW (+v, 331°) veranda and SSE (-v, 151°) low porch. The final inventory has exactly one door, on +v, matching the sheet without duplication. However, neither its principal status nor access beneath the opposite canopy is established; correct porch placement does not verify the principal entrance.

building.summary: Recognizable brown-and-cream miniature with convincing connected wings, but the characteristic roof dormer needs repair.

SV2 establishes the separate cream door on the SE (-u) steep-roof gable, matching the rendered door at 135°. The inventory contains these two distinct entrances, not duplicated principal portals; wing handedness also matches.

scene.summary: The steep gable, connected L-shaped wings, low hipped connector and brown-and-cream palette are recognizable and cohesive. The +v dormer remains visibly blank rather than showing its characteristic broad three-window face; do not count that repair as visually resolved.

orientation.summary: The final two-door inventory and sheets match the prior independent findings: sheltered blue principal entrance on SW (-v, 225°), and separate cream Elm Lane entrance on SE (-u, 135°). These are distinct supported entrances, not duplicated principal portals; wing handedness remains consistent.

building.summary: The asymmetric wings, muted hipped roofs, pale siding and restrained trim make a coherent, charming miniature. No obvious modeling defects are visible, but principal-entry placement remains unverified.

orientation.summary: The labeled sheet and actual door inventory agree on one sheltered entrance on -u (SW, 222°), with no duplicated principal portal. However, SV2 looks southeast toward -u/-v through heavy vegetation and does not establish a doorway. SV1 faces +u/-v; SV3–4 face -v, not +v, and are similarly obscured. The north-up aerial supports the asymmetric roof massing but cannot locate the entrance. Neither the nearest road nor the author's provisional plan verifies -u.

issues.problem: The sole principal entrance is modeled on -u without visible reference confirmation.
issues.fix: Obtain a clearly located view showing the entrance and its relationship to the roof wings; retain or relocate the single sheltered portal accordingly before approval.

scene.summary: Asymmetric wings, low gray hip roofs, pale siding and modest trim form a convincing small miniature. No conspicuous architectural rendering defect is evident, but unresolved principal-entry placement prevents approval.

orientation.summary: The sheet and final inventory agree on one sheltered SW door (-u, 222°), without duplication. Prior independent source-to-face findings establish that the vegetation-obscured views do not locate an entrance; the aerial supports massing only. The provisional author plan supplies no new verification.

building.summary: The miniature has a coherent, simple single-storey silhouette and no obvious visible defects, but the target’s entrance cannot be verified through the vegetation.

orientation.summary: The face sheet and actual inventory agree on one door at -v (SW, 225°), with no duplicated principal portals. SV1/SV3 look southeast toward +u (NW), not +v; SV2/SV4 view +u and obliquely -v, but foliage obscures the target. Neither the map nor aerial establishes an entrance on -v. The visible brown shed cannot safely be identified as the mapped target.

issues.problem: The sole principal entrance is provisionally placed on -v without visible source confirmation, preventing orientation approval.
issues.fix: Obtain a clear, geolocated view of the target’s entrance and map its outward bearing to the labeled faces; retain or relocate the single door accordingly.

scene.summary: The narrow single-storey mass, shallow longitudinal gable and restrained siding and trim read clearly at diorama scale. No obvious modeling defect is visible, but the sole entrance remains unsupported.

orientation.summary: The final inventory and sheet show exactly one SW side door (-v, 225°). Prior independent findings place the source views mainly toward +u, with only oblique -v visibility through foliage; they do not establish this doorway, and the visible brown shed is not securely identified as the target. No duplicate exists, but principal-entry orientation remains unresolved.

building.summary: Recognizable and stylistically coherent, with correctly handed garages and balcony, but the Elm-facing roof and chimney need stronger reference fidelity.

orientation.summary: SV1’s oblique view shows entry stairs on the SW (+u) side near the Gebbie end, consistent with the rendered +u entrance and actual door inventory. SV4 looks NW toward the SE (-v) garage facade, with pedestrian access around its left corner. SV3 looks SE toward NW (+v), confirming balcony access on the left and a secondary door and garage on the right. These match the labeled renders; no duplicated principal portal is evident.

issues.problem: The Elm-facing elevation loses its defining broad, tall chimney beside the balcony. A tiny ridge stack and dominant plain gable replace the reference’s substantial chimney and low hipped balcony roof.
issues.fix: Restore a broad siding-clad chimney rising beside the balcony and reshape the balcony roof into the lower hipped form shown in SV3. Preserve the right-hand garage wing.

issues.problem: The Gebbie gable glazing reads as four ordinary rectangular windows rather than the distinctive roof-following glazed composition in SV4.
issues.fix: Shape the upper paired panes to follow the gable slopes and emphasize the cream central mullion and surrounding frame.

scene.summary: The articulated gray massing, cream trim, raised open-railed balcony and correctly handed garages are recognizable and fit the scene’s scale. However, the final sheet still shows a tiny ridge stack instead of the characteristic broad, tall chimney beside the Elm-facing balcony; the dominant plain gable also leaves the requested lower hipped balcony-roof silhouette unresolved. Gebbie-facing glazing remains four rectangular panes rather than roof-following paired glazing. Despite the repair-applied flag, these visual improvements are not demonstrated. No obvious floating or broken geometry is visible.

orientation.summary: The final door inventory and labeled views agree with the prior independent findings: the principal stair-served entrance is on SW (+u), near the Gebbie end; NW (+v) has secondary balcony access and a separate pedestrian door beside the right-hand garage; SE (-v) has the Gebbie garage, with pedestrian access around its left corner. No duplicated principal entrance is evident. This conclusion follows the prior source-to-face findings and actual doors, not the author plan or nearest-road hint.

building.summary: Recognizable colors and twin-gabled frontage, but characteristic porch shapes and the roof silhouette need refinement.

issues.problem: The Pratt entrance’s distinctive broad curved canopy and substantial stone-based porch have become a small angular awning with slender supports.

scene.summary: Cedar-brown siding, cream trim, twin entrance gables, purple door, curved upper accent, and recessed rear wings make this recognizable. Projecting gables enliven the roof silhouette, though long rear roof slabs remain dominant. The Pratt entrance still reads as a shallow angular canopy rather than the distinctive broad arch; its stone landing and pier bases need greater visual weight. The Oak veranda retains a low, blank pediment without a discernible vent and still resembles stacked balconies rather than a deep sheltered porch. These are targeted silhouette refinements, not a request for photographic reconstruction. Materials and window scale are coherent, with no obvious floating or broken geometry.

orientation.summary: The prior independent SV4 finding places the principal entrance on -v (SW, 219°). building.summary: Recognizable gabled cottage with the characteristic elevated rose veranda and garage below. The oversized staircase needs correction.

issues.problem: The plain cream canopy loses the distinctive striped awning treatment visible in SV2/SV3.
issues.fix: Add restrained cream-and-tan stripes and a short hanging valance while keeping the veranda open.

scene.summary: The front gable, white rake trim, apex vent, rose veranda and garage below give this cottage a distinctive silhouette. Although the repair is recorded as applied, the final four-face sheet still shows a broad, solid cream staircase without visible protective handrails; the intended compact rose-toned stair and landing are not evident. Narrow the flight and add rose supports and connected railings. Restrained canopy stripes and a short valance would improve character but are secondary.

orientation.summary: Prior independent SV2 findings establish the entrance porch facing -u (NNW, 340°), toward Peck Avenue. building.summary: Recognizable, coherent miniature: the shallow gray hip roof, pale clapboard, sage shutters and paired two-storey northwest bays capture the house well. No obvious major defects.

scene.summary: The compact hip-roof silhouette, pale clapboard, sage shutters and paired northwest bays remain recognizable and coherent. The hooded entrance and steps read well; no major visible defects.

orientation.summary: Prior independent MAP/SV3 findings establish the southwest entrance on +v (220°). The final sheet and actual inventory agree: exactly one door, centered on +v. Northwest bays remain windows, not duplicated entrances.

building.summary: Recognizable and stylistically coherent, with a convincing front porch and sunroom. The prominent side gable needs its defining attic detail.
